elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 states that the Company owns all right, title and interest in the Site, including its design, look and feel and all other deliverables and work product created for the Company.

elements.element: Customer's ownership of the deliverables and work product is effected through an assignment by Vendor.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly “hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest” in the Site and the other deliverables and work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: The assignment expressly excludes HDI's pre-existing and generally applicable software, tools, platform and know-how, “which HDI retains.”

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI grants the Company a licence to the retained HDI materials to the extent embedded in, or necessary to use, the Site and deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as “perpetual.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as “irrevocable.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as “royalty-free.”

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Company retains all right, title and interest in materials, data and information supplied on its behalf and in all customer, user and order data collected through the Site; the clause also states that no Company data is transferred to HDI.

elements.element: No joint ownership of intellectual property is created.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 expressly states that “no joint or co-ownership of any intellectual property is created.”

elements.element: Vendor owns all generic tools.
elements.evidence: HDI retains only tools that are both “pre-existing and generally applicable.” The clause does not clearly reserve to HDI generic tools developed during the engagement, which may instead fall within assigned work product.

elements.element: Vendor owns all generic know-how.
elements.evidence: The retention is limited to HDI's “pre-existing and generally applicable” know-how and does not clearly cover generic know-how developed during the engagement.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence covering the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company receives ownership of the deliverables, while the express licence covers only retained HDI materials embedded in or necessary to use them. There is no express licence whose object is the deliverables themselves.

elements.element: The licence covering the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The perpetual term applies to the licence for retained HDI materials, not to a licence covering the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence covering the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The irrevocable term applies to the licence for retained HDI materials, not to a licence covering the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence covering the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The worldwide term applies to the licence for retained HDI materials, not to a licence covering the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence covering the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The royalty-free term applies to the licence for retained HDI materials, not to a licence covering the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company owns the deliverables and therefore has broader practical use rights, but the express licensed right to use applies only to retained HDI materials.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The express modification right applies to retained HDI materials, not to the deliverables as the licensed subject matter.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The express sublicensing right applies to retained HDI materials, not to the deliverables as the licensed subject matter.

elements.element: The licensed rights in the deliverables may be exercised for Customer's business.
elements.evidence: The business-purpose language limits the licence for retained HDI materials; it does not qualify an express licence covering the deliverables.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position through an express assignment, a background-IP carveout and embedded-IP licence, comprehensive Company-data ownership, and a no-joint-ownership statement. It does not independently implement the fallback structure: the generic-tools and know-how reservation is limited to pre-existing assets, and the express licence is directed to retained HDI materials rather than to the deliverables. Although Company ownership gives broader practical rights in the deliverables, it is not the specified deliverables licence. The edit preserves the existing commercial provisions, but it is not minimal because it adds worldwide, modification, sublicensing and business-purpose terms beyond those needed for the preferred position.
